gap: No result ChatGPT got (of the four I could read) states a per-dollar or per-pound capacity figure for any 10,000 mAh built-in-cable bank; the best I could source is the Anker Nano A1638 at $4.60 per 1,000 rated mAh at today's $45.99 against the Anker Zolo's $3.00, plus the A1638's cable falling from 45 W to 15 W when its spare USB-C port is also in use.
standout_why: Compared against Talk Android (cited), Anker's best-power-bank blog (cited), Pickstead and TechRadar. Talk Android gives list price, mAh and output only, with no Wh, input watts, phone-charge count or any derived figure. Anker's blog gives the A1638's 2-hour recharge and 45 W / 40 W phone figures, with no price, weight or Wh. Pickstead already has part of this angle: the 'capacity x 0.65 / phone battery' rule and the Zolo's 5,500-7,000 mAh delivered range. TechRadar's page came back truncated before any product entry, so I could not compare it; Best Buy and Popular Science were not opened. The derived figures are new but cover Anker's three models only: us.ugreen.com, baseus.com and iniushop.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so nothing could be computed for the UGREEN, Baseus or INIU banks.
decides: It does not decide the pick. On sourced inputs it only confirms the A1638 is not the value choice even at today's $45.99 (ChatGPT showed $59.99): $4.60 per 1,000 rated mAh against the Zolo's $3.00, and its 45 W holds for one device only. The UGREEN Nexode Pro 10K and Baseus FC11 10K are both $35.99 in the brief's partner-store table, which would be $3.60 per 1,000 mAh, but I did not open those pages and have no Wh, weight, input or PPS figure for them. Another agent must read those before either can be ranked.
